rule: Edit only copy and SEO fields on existing pages (meta title, meta description, heading text, heading tag with its size rule, paragraphs, FAQ question and answer text, schema); never add, remove, move or restyle a section, change a layout or build a page: send those to Beckett.
why: Every structural change on a client site has been Beckett's call; the FSO rule is that only header, links, copy, colours and images change, and Yard Dogs' re-shaped buttons (Sep 2026) were caught by him.
check: The planned diff touches only text-bearing settings (title, editor, tab_title, tab_content, rank_math_*, schema); any change to elements[] structure, custom_css, typography or a new post id aborts the push.

rule: Never touch WordPress settings outside SEO copy: no plugin installs or removals, caching config, theme or plugin PHP, analytics or tracking IDs, blog_public, permalink structure, user accounts or the Elementor Kit.
why: Beckett, WesCo (Sep 2026): "The skill should never touch WordPress setting stuff"; those belong to Beckett or the dev.
check: The WRITE-SCOPE options list contains only rank-math-options-titles keys explicitly approved for this job; anything else is rejected before the run.

rule: Do not edit or move the "Painting in Colorado + Florida" block on Elevation's home page.
why: It is the old home page's content, word for word, and carries 85 of the 89 rankings (sweep 12 Oct 2026).
check: Element ids of that block are on a protected list; any diff touching them aborts.

rule: Never swap one template section for another, or replace a global shortcode block with a per-page copy (or the reverse), on your own call.
why: Elevation's market homes got Sunshine's town grid in place of the template's toggle and Beckett asked "When did I authorize that" (13 Oct 2026); globals stay globals.
check: Element count, widget types and every [elementor-template id=...] shortcode on the page are identical before and after the push.

rule: Treat any wp_options write (Rank Math identity, esci_* contact options) as a disclosed exception: name it in the scope file and on its own line in the report.
why: Some option writes are required (esci phone override, og:site_name) but the settings guardrail says they get their own line every time.
check: The push report lists every option written by name; an option write not in WRITE-SCOPE.json fails the guard.

rule: If schema or tracking is hard-coded in theme PHP, a child theme or GTM, do not edit it: report where it lives and escalate.
why: ProWash's old agency schema lived in content.php/content-page.php and GTM and blocked the new Rank Math schema (May 2026); the PHP edit was not Tamim's to make.
check: grep the rendered HTML for a second ld+json block that Rank Math did not emit; if found, the tool reports its source instead of writing.

rule: On a site that launched under SEO preserve, make no on-page changes for 4 to 6 weeks, then change one variable at a time.
why: Tamim's own rule from the Yard Dogs doc, applied to Elevation (launched 22 Oct 2026, re-sweep 29 Oct): if rankings move you must know why.
check: The tool refuses a push on a site whose launch date in the site config is under 28 days old unless Beckett overrides; one change set per page per sweep cycle.

rule: Note out-of-scope problems you find and report them; never fix them in passing.
why: FSO stage 8 rule: execute the approved work order and nothing else, so every change on a client site has an owner.
check: The push report has a FOUND, NOT FIXED section; the diff contains only the planned rows.

rule: Never add a block that already exists on the page (a second FAQ, trust strip or location block) to get more keywords in.
why: Mehedi declined to duplicate a services block on ProWash for duplicate content (May 2026) and Beckett agreed.
check: Count H2 texts per page before and after; no H2 text appears twice.

rule: Never create legal pages, new pages or new posts; a write that creates a post needs allow_new_posts, which is Beckett's.
why: Eight sites have no legal pages and Beckett parked them ("market-wide PP and TOS later", 22 Sep 2026); page creation is his.
check: WRITE-SCOPE.json has allow_new_posts false; the guard aborts any wp_insert_post.

rule: Run every write with SCOPE=<WRITE-SCOPE.json> listing the exact post ids and option names, approved before the run, and every read with READONLY=1.
why: The write guard exists because unscoped writes damaged live pages; eval-file with neither declaration is blocked by the hook.
check: The command line carries SCOPE= or READONLY=1; the server log prints "WRITE GUARD active" and "N write(s) made, all in scope".

rule: Take `wp db export` before every write session and keep a per-page revert JSON of _elementor_data plus the rank_math pair.
why: Every recovery so far (Dobbins clone scrub hitting Yard Dogs, restored in 2 minutes on 5 Oct 2026) depended on a backup taken first.
check: A dated .sql in ~/hhl-backups and one REVERT file per touched post exist before the first write of the session.

rule: On Elevation (and any pipeline-built site), edit pages only through `seo push`: it stamps each page _seo_live_edited, and the build push.php skips stamped pages. Never hand-edit in Elementor or wp-admin.
why: Before 23 Oct a hand edit was erased by the next build push with no warning; the stamp + skip closes that, but only for edits made through the kit.
check: locate.php shows live_edited on the page after a push; push.php logs 'skip <path>: live-edited' on the next build run.

rule: After anyone edits a page in wp-admin, change it only with targeted ops on the LIVE data; never re-push a whole page compiled from an older pull.
why: Yard Dogs (30 Sep 2026): a late copy change nearly wiped the form webhooks Beckett had just mapped in wp-admin.
check: The push reads the page's current _elementor_data at run time and writes only the planned element ids; the post_modified time is compared to the last pull and a newer edit stops the run.

rule: Dry-run every multi-page or site-wide change and read the scope report before applying it.
why: A live search-replace with no dry run damaged the About page heading; the hook now blocks it.
check: Every push has a DRY=1 pass that prints post id, element id, field, old value, new value; zero NOT FOUND rows before the real run.

rule: Keep copy as data (a JSON or sheet of page, element id, field, new value) and generate the write from it; never hand-type copy into a PHP script.
why: The Sunshine and Elevation fills only stayed consistent because copy came from one structured source (services-copy.py, make_fill.py).
check: Every changed value in the push traces to a row in the change file.

rule: Say what you did not do in the same breath as "done" ("done except X").
why: Ridgeline: "the project posts are done" was said while all six still read Bonita Springs, Florida.
check: The push report ends with a DEFERRED list, empty or not.

rule: Read the whole list before claiming something does not exist (post types, menus, templates, redirects).
why: A truncated `wp post-type list` produced a confident wrong claim that a CPT was missing.
check: Use --format=json/csv with no pager and count rows before saying "none".

rule: After two failed blind fixes, stop and instrument (or escalate) instead of trying a third.
why: Sunshine (Aug 2026): two Chromium-based mobile fixes made the live site worse, one locked iOS scrolling.
check: A fix attempt counter per issue in the session notes; at 2, the next step is diagnosis, not a write.

rule: Log every new miss as one line in the misses ledger or fix ledger, written as a default for next time.
why: Beckett (30 Sep 2026): "all these mistakes we caught, this should never happen again."
check: Each incident in the session has a matching ledger row before the session ends.

rule: Commit only the client paths you changed (`git add <paths>`), never `git commit -am`.
why: Yard Dogs (30 Sep 2026): commit -am swept other projects' files in the shared workspace.
check: git status before commit shows only the intended client folder staged.

rule: Reach a client site only through its row in ~/HHL/sites.json and `wpsite <key>`; if the site is not there, fingerprint the host and ask Beckett for the one missing piece.
why: The registry is the single source of truth (19 Sep 2026) and wpsite runs the write guard on the exact command it builds.
check: `wpsite list` shows the key; the command used is `wpsite <key> ...`, never a hand-typed ssh.

rule: Never edit the Cloudways copies of Sunset (app 6324586) or Legacy (app 6324601): the live sites are on GHL hosting.
why: Both Cloudways apps are old copies; edits there change nothing a visitor sees and can be mistaken for the live site.
check: `wp option get home` on the target matches the live domain before any write.

rule: Confirm the target app by its home URL and sys_user before writing; never select an app by "newest" or by name match.
why: Dobbins (5 Oct 2026): a script took the newest app on the shared server and started scrubbing Yard Dogs' staging site.
check: `wp option get home` and the sys_user printed at the top of every write run equal the sites.json row.

rule: Write through `wp eval-file` (WP-CLI), never the REST API.
why: On GHL hosting app-password REST writes are capability-stripped even for an admin (Sunshine, 10 Aug 2026); WP-CLI runs as system.
check: No POST/PUT to /wp-json/ in the tool; writes appear in the guard log.

rule: Put config files for server-side scripts in ~/tmp on the server: wpsite does not pass local environment variables through.
why: Sunset market stamp (Oct 2026): scripts read ~/tmp/*.json on the server because env vars never arrived.
check: The script logs the config path it read and its contents hash.

rule: Keep MCP connectors and Novamira off production writes; production writes are SSH + WP-CLI only.
why: A community MCP returned HTTP 200 and "success" while the page went blank (research, Oct 2026).
check: No MCP tool call in the push path.

rule: On GHL-hosted WordPress add --skip-plugins=novamira to every wp command.
why: Novamira fatals under the CLI's PHP 7.4 ("unexpected ':'") on Sunshine, Legacy and Sunset; without the flag every command dies with a critical error.
check: The wpsite helper adds the flag for GHL rows; a command output containing "critical error" stops the run.

rule: After a write on GHL hosting, purge GHL's edge: the site's mu-plugin `CDN_Clear_Cache_Api::cache_api_call([],"purge_everything")` where configured, otherwise ask Beckett to press GHL panel > Advanced Settings > Cache management > Clear Cache.
why: GHL's Cloudflare caches HTML with s-maxage 30 days; Bespoke's drafted blog stayed public until the panel purge (16 Oct 2026). The mu-plugin is inert without CDN_SITE_ID/CDN_SITE_TOKEN in wp-config (Legacy has them).
check: Plain-URL fetch after the purge shows the new text and a small age header.

rule: Do not set headers, caching or page rules in the client's own Cloudflare zone for a GHL-hosted site: that zone is not in the request path.
why: Sunshine (24 Aug 2026): zone settings were accepted and read back but never reached a visitor; GHL fronts with its own Cloudflare.
check: A static upload URL does not carry the setting; put origin-level changes in an mu-plugin instead (escalate).

rule: To hide a blog on GHL WordPress, unset Settings > Reading > Posts page (page_for_posts 0) as well as drafting the page, then clear the GHL edge.
why: Bespoke (16 Oct 2026): a drafted Posts page stays public because WordPress ignores draft status for it.
check: Plain URL of the old blog returns 404 after the edge purge.

rule: Never run two crawlers at the same time against a GHL-hosted site.
why: Sunset (14 Oct 2026): parallel crawls got 429s and the results had to be thrown away.
check: The verify step crawls sequentially with a delay; any 429 marks the run invalid.

rule: On Cloudways, verify that Seraphinite's host map matches the live domain; after a domain change it must be rebuilt (seraph-dropin.php) or nothing is cached or optimised.
why: Yard Dogs (30 Sep 2026): the clone kept the donor host in advanced-cache.php, mobile PageSpeed sat at 60 until the drop-in was rebuilt.
check: Home HTML contains `seraph_accel_gi` and `data-lzl-src`; clean-check area 22 passes.

rule: A 500 on save is usually the server memory limit: stop and escalate, do not retry the write in a loop.
why: Mehedi (10 Jul 2026): "This problem comes from low memory."
check: Any 500 from a write stops the run and reports.

rule: After every write purge every layer in serving order: Elementor CSS + object cache, then Seraphinite's page cache, then Cloudways Varnish, then Cloudflare if it caches HTML.
why: Ridgeline showed corrected stats to every cache-busted check and the old stats to Beckett for 46 minutes; WesCo served the previous client's homepage for hours from 903 Seraphinite files.
check: `scripts/purge.sh` output shows all four steps; the first plain request after it is x-cache MISS with age 0.

rule: Send Varnish PURGE with the site's Host header (`-H "Host: <domain>"`), per URL, or with X-Purge-Method: regex for the whole site. (Since 26 Oct 2026 Varnish is OFF on our Cloudways server: Seraphinite is the only page cache. On GHL hosting the layer above Seraphinite is GHL's Rocket.net CDN: purge it with the site panel's Clear Cache.)
why: Dobbins (15 Oct 2026): PURGE to 127.0.0.1:8080 without Host returned 200 and purged nothing; the client saw a 40-hour-old page.
check: After PURGE, the plain URL returns x-cache MISS (or a small age) and the new text.

rule: Purge Seraphinite per URL with `seraph_accel\API::OperateCache(2, "<full url>")`; a post id does nothing.
why: Elevation About team edit (16 Oct 2026) stayed stale until the full-URL call plus a Varnish PURGE with Host.
check: The plain URL serves the edited text after the call.

rule: Remember `wp cache flush` clears only the WordPress object cache, not the page cache visitors get.
why: Ridgeline (Aug 2026): object cache flushed, Varnish kept serving the pre-edit HTML.
check: Headers on the plain URL, not the flush exit code, decide whether the change is live.

rule: After writing _elementor_data, clear that post's generated CSS and element cache (`wp elementor flush-css`, or delete its _elementor_css and _elementor_element_cache meta).
why: Elementor can serve a page's element tree and CSS from its own cache, so the DB changes while the page does not; Elevation's spelling pass deletes _elementor_css after each write.
check: Rendered HTML of the post contains the new text after the flush and before any page-cache purge question arises.

rule: Warm the cache one page at a time (about 2 seconds apart) after a full purge, never in parallel.
why: A parallel warm of 11 pages on a cold Cloudways site drove load to 9.5 and pages timed out right before a hand-off.
check: `warm.sh` runs sequentially; every second hit under 0.6 s.

rule: If cf-cache-status is HIT on HTML, Cloudflare needs its own purge; our token cannot purge, so tell Beckett.
why: CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN has no Cache Purge permission (8 Oct 2026); DYNAMIC means Cloudflare is not the problem.
check: Read cf-cache-status on the plain URL; HIT triggers a message, not a silent pass.

rule: After a slug change, flush Rank Math's sitemap cache (delete the %rank_math_sitemap% option rows and call Cache::invalidate_storage()).
why: Sunshine (27 Aug 2026): the Rank Math sitemap kept listing stale slugs long after the change.
check: post-sitemap.xml / page-sitemap.xml list the new slug and not the old one.

rule: Verify every change on the PLAIN canonical URL a visitor hits, never on a ?cb= or any query-string URL.
why: A query string bypasses Seraphinite and Varnish, so it proves the DB and nothing else; a stale homepage shipped twice this way (Ridgeline 46 min, WesCo hours).
check: curl the exact canonical URL (Safari user agent) and confirm the new text plus x-cache/age headers; if plain and cache-busted disagree, the plain one is the truth.

rule: Read every write back from the database AND from the rendered page; a script's success log or a 200 is never proof.
why: A tool that reports "35 elements updated / NOT FOUND: none" only proves it found the 35 it was asked for (Ridgeline); a vendor 200 has lied repeatedly.
check: Per changed field: DB value equals the planned value, and the stripped rendered text contains it.

rule: Report DB presence and rendered presence separately, and count only published posts, never revisions.
why: Legacy (11 Aug 2026): an asbestos licence was called "live and public" off a DB hit with zero hits on the page; "1,023 rows" was about 768 revisions, the real number was 92.
check: Every count in a report says which layer and filters post_status='publish'.

rule: Grep the tag-stripped rendered text for visible copy, and the raw HTML for text hiding in attributes, CSS content:, and JSON-LD.
why: Sunshine copy hid in attributes, body classes and JSON-LD where a human never looked; a CSS ::after printed "Serving Southwest Florida" that no text grep saw (Ridgeline).
check: Two greps per page: stripped text and raw HTML including `content:` and ld+json.

rule: When capturing page text, open every accordion and tab and harvest each panel as it opens.
why: WesCo landscaping page: all 5 FAQ questions and 4 of 5 answers were missing from the capture; about 100 text slots sitewide were invisible to the gate.
check: Captured text includes every tab_title and tab_content of every accordion on the page.

rule: Never judge a visibility or animation bug from a headless or background browser.
why: The "blank hero" bug (Aug 2026) was a measurement artifact: IntersectionObserver never fires in a hidden pane; real devices were fine.
check: Confirm on a visibly painting viewport or a real device before reporting.

rule: Use headless Playwright for site checks, never Beckett's own browser.
why: Standing rule: site checks must not take over his Chrome or screen.
check: The verify step launches its own browser context.

rule: Read the sitemap's slugs (post-sitemap.xml, page-sitemap.xml) after any rewrite, not just the pages.
why: Sunshine (Aug 2026): 8 blog posts were windows content on roofing URLs for months because reviewers read titles and the sitemap holds URLs.
check: Every slug in the sitemaps matches its page's current topic; no donor trade words in any slug.

rule: Run the language audit after every copy push: em dashes, British spellings, repeated words, placeholders, periods.
why: WesCo shipped "neighbourhoods" and "kerb" on a Florida site and four review agents missed both.
check: `python3 scripts/language-audit.py <url> --extra <paths>` reports zero findings on the touched pages.

rule: Check blog_public = 1 and no noindex meta on the live domain whenever you audit a launched site; never change it yourself.
why: WesCo (10 Sep 2026) went live with blog_public still 0, a finished site telling Google to index nothing.
check: `wp option get blog_public` returns 1 on the live host and the home HTML has no noindex robots meta; a 0 is escalated.

rule: After a rank-holding launch, re-sweep with the same seo.config.json one week later and, for any lost ranking, compare that page to its preserve list first.
why: The SEO FSO track (Yard Dogs, Elevation re-sweep 29 Oct 2026) depends on a before/after on identical searches.
check: A diff of sweep.json before vs after, per keyword, with the page's preserve rows beside each loss.

rule: Count headings on the rendered page at both 1440 and 390, because some themes print a different block per breakpoint.
why: Yard Dogs' old theme rendered sections twice (desktop and mobile copies), doubling raw heading counts.
check: Heading inventory taken from visible elements only, per breakpoint.

rule: Never change a heading's tag (H1/H2/H3) without keeping its size: template size rules target the tag (`selector h1`, `selector h2`), so a tag swap changes the rendered size.
why: Elevation launch (22 Oct 2026): the hero heading demoted for SEO rendered at 62px instead of 35px on phones; 577 tag-bound rules exist sitewide.
check: After the push, the computed font-size and line count of the changed heading at 390 and 1440 equal the values before the push (or the same section on a sibling page).

rule: When a heading tag changes, the widget's custom CSS selector must be re-aimed to the new tag in the same change; if the tool cannot do that safely, escalate instead of swapping the tag.
why: Tamim's May 2026 hero H1 changes broke sizes on market, about and service pages until Mehedi swapped `h2` to `h1` in the CSS; batch fix on Legacy, Cold Iron and Mako 23 May.
check: The widget's custom_css references the new tag after the push, and the font-size check above passes.

rule: Keep exactly one H1 per page.
why: Duplicated pages without _elementor_page_settings print the WP page title as a second H1 (Ridgeline); HHL's own WP home once had 5 H1s used as section labels.
check: Count `<h1>` in the rendered HTML of every touched page: always 1.

rule:
Keep the accent (and any
) inside a heading when you rewrite its text; write `Simple as 1-2-3`, not the plain string.
why: About 15 headings lost their accent word on WesCo when plain text was written over the span (Aug 2026).
check: The number of <span> in each changed heading equals the number before; spans and closing tags balance.

rule: Make the H1 the exact target keyword with no selling words in front; selling words and the phone go in the meta title and description.
why: Tamim's rule (30 Jul 2026); "FL" and "Florida" are treated the same and the abbreviation keeps titles short.
check: The H1 text matches the page's target keyword from the keyword map with no extra words.

rule: On ProWash the service hero H1 is the page title and the excerpt is the paragraph under it; changing the H1 means changing post_title, and they cannot differ there.
why: Mehedi (10 May 2026): the ProWash template reads the title into the hero; a separate H1 needs a template rebuild.
check: On ProWash service pages, rendered H1 equals post_title after the push.

rule: Write headings in sentence case and check the rendered text: template CSS (`text-transform: capitalize`) or Rank Math capitalize_titles can turn "in" into "In".
why: Yard Dogs ("And Surrounding Areas", 30 Sep 2026) and Dobbins ("In Boca", 5 Oct 2026).
check: Rendered innerText of the heading equals the written string, case included.

rule: No heading takes a period; every paragraph and sentence-like line does.
why: House rule from the language pass (8 Sep 2026); a client caught a descriptive line with no period under a heading.
check: language-audit.py punctuation check clean on the touched page.

rule: Never open two pages with the same H2.
why: Beckett ruling on LCC (15 Sep 2026): keep it on the page it belongs to, use another of the client's lines on the second.
check: Site-wide H2 inventory has no duplicate first-section H2.

rule: Keep heading levels in order (no skipped rung) and give each sub-service one H3 with 60 to 120 words under it.
why: Site audit HEAD family flags skipped levels; Tamim's sub-service rule for Elevation (12 Oct 2026).
check: Rendered outline: H1 then H2s then H3s with no H2 to H4 jump; word count under each sub-service H3 in range.

rule:
Keep a rewritten heading close to the old one's length; line breaks come from the widget's max width, not
.
why: Mehedi: copy length is a layout input ("If you write a big word like average there then it will not work"); a long heading can stack one word per line (LCC ruling).
check: Rendered line count of the heading at 390 and 1440 is no more than one line above the original.

rule: Rank Math settings live in hyphen-named options (rank-math-options-titles, rank-math-options-general); merge single keys, never write the whole option.
why: Yard Dogs (30 Sep 2026): the first scrub used the wrong names and only reset knowledgegraph_name; a whole-option write wipes the array.
check: Read the option before and after: only the planned keys changed, key count unchanged.

rule: Set rank_math_title and rank_math_description explicitly on every page you touch; never leave the description empty.
why: Empty descriptions fall back to %excerpt% or post_content, which held donor copy (Yard Dogs "Veteran-owned ... Bradenton", Sunshine's Fort Myers page sharing as "Collier County").
check: Both meta keys are non-empty after the push and the rendered <title> and meta description equal them.

rule: Copy preserved titles and meta descriptions verbatim on a rank-holding site; the only approved edits are the ones on the preserve list.
why: Yard Dogs and Elevation: Google titles and descriptions carried word for word (one approved change: a dash to a pipe on the Yard Dogs home).
check: Diff rendered title/description against SEO-PRESERVE.md for every preserved page: identical.

rule: Keep Rank Math capitalize_titles off.
why: With it on, client exact titles change ("in" becomes "In"), which matters on rank-holding sites (Yard Dogs).
check: `rank-math-options-titles.capitalize_titles` = off on every site the tool touches.

rule: Keep titles under about 62 characters and unique per page; never "Home" or a placeholder.
why: Site audit HEAD family flags titles over 62; Elevation's sitecheck asserts unique titles.
check: Rendered <title> length <= 62 and no two pages share a title.

rule: Remember post_excerpt is printed by card grids on the home and hub pages, not on the page you are editing.
why: Ridgeline/Sunshine: wrong excerpts showed in the home services grid while the page itself looked right.
check: After an excerpt change, fetch the pages whose card grid lists that page and find the new text.

rule: Set og:image per page through rank_math_facebook_image_id (the id beats the url), with homepage_facebook_image and open_graph_image as the fallbacks.
why: Setting only the URL changes nothing; Rank Math falls back to the featured image, which put a WesCo photo in Yard Dogs' iMessage preview (30 Sep 2026).
check: Rendered og:image on the page equals the planned image; test with a fresh URL since iMessage and Facebook cache hard.

rule: Leave deliberate noindex on demo or filler posts (rank_math_robots noindex) alone.
why: Clone-carried blog posts ship noindex on purpose; Rank Math drops them from the sitemap.
check: Do not include rank_math_robots in a push unless Beckett asked.

rule: Never write schema into Elementor Custom Code (_elementor_code) with update_post_meta from the CLI; write it with a direct guarded $wpdb update, read it back, and assert `<script` is present and the JSON parses.
why: Mako (19 Oct 2026): the CLI write ran as user 0 without unfiltered_html, the script wrapper was stripped and raw schema JSON printed on every page; kses_remove_filters() did not stop it.
check: After the push, crawl every URL using that snippet: stripped visible text contains no "@context", and the ld+json block parses.

rule: After any schema change, look at the rendered page top to bottom before calling it done.
why: Tamim (15 May 2026): a stray character before the script tag printed text above the header.
check: No text node outside <script> contains `{`, `@type` or `@context`; header area screenshot unchanged.

rule: Check that the JSON-LD @graph names the client (knowledgegraph_name, website_name, logo and its _id, phones, address) and not a donor.
why: Ridgeline (12 Aug 2026): the <title> said Ridgeline while @graph still said Sunshine State Windows with the donor logo.
check: Parse the rendered ld+json and grep for every donor name, phone and domain: zero.

rule: On a multi-market site emit one LocalBusiness (trade type) per market with that market's NAP, on that market's pages only.
why: Elevation (Oct 2026): HousePainter per market via the ep-seo.php mu-plugin; a site-wide single NAP would put Colorado's phone on Florida pages.
check: On each market page, the schema telephone and address equal that market's config.

rule: Do not add a second schema source on top of an existing one; find and report every emitter (Rank Math, Elementor Custom Code snippets, mu-plugins, theme, GTM).
why: Elevation still carried Sunset's sitewide RoofingContractor snippet #7332 until it was drafted; ProWash's old schema blocked the new one.
check: Count ld+json blocks and their @type per page: no duplicate LocalBusiness, no donor type.

rule: On Elevation, change market schema through the build's seo layer (ep-seo.php), not Rank Math's per-page schema.
why: The HousePainter blocks are emitted by an mu-plugin pushed by seo.php; Rank Math schema on top would duplicate them.
check: The diff touches the seo layer source, and the page still has exactly one HousePainter.

rule: On a rank-holding launch, keep the old schema identity as it was even where it disagrees with the new footer; fix it later as its own change.
why: Yard Dogs schema hours said Mon to Sun 9 to 5 while the footer said Mon to Fri 8 to 6; the rule was hold, don't fix.
check: Schema identity fields equal the old site's crawl until the hold period ends.

rule: Allow 24 hours or more for new schema to show in the validator before redoing anything.
why: Tamim (14 May 2026) on Sunset and Legacy local schema.
check: Validator recheck scheduled for the next day, not repeated edits.

rule: Check post_author and licence numbers in schema: a donor author slug or a licence with the wrong trade prefix is a leftover.
why: SunsetTamim123 leaked into /author/ in schema on Sunshine; a CCC (roofing) licence rode along on a window company (CBC building, CGC general).
check: Parse author and licence values in the rendered schema; compare to the client's confirmed facts.

rule: Before editing a FAQ, find out if it is a global template (`[elementor-template id=9182]` or 2873) or a per-page accordion; editing the global changes every page that embeds it.
why: On the FSO templates the FAQ is one library template pulled in by shortcode; Tamim hit this on Legacy service pages (5 to 8 May 2026).
check: Resolve the FAQ's post id from the page's shortcode; the scope report lists every page that embeds it before the write.

rule: Confirm an accordion is actually the FAQ before writing to it; the accordion under a hero is often an explainer.
why: Sunshine (Aug 2026): the under-hero explainer accordion was mapped as FAQ and clobbered, palette swatches included.
check: Dump id, widget type and tab titles and match them to the rendered FAQ heading before the push.

rule: Unique FAQs per page is the SEO goal, but turning a global FAQ into per-page FAQs is a structural change: escalate it.
why: Tamim and Beckett (4 May 2026): global FAQs across pages are bad for SEO; free sites ship one global FAQ and per-page FAQs come with the SEO upgrade.
check: A request for a page-specific FAQ on a page that embeds a global FAQ produces an escalation, not a write.

rule: Edit FAQ items in the accordion's repeater (`settings.tabs[i].tab_title` and `tab_content`), keeping item count and order unless asked.
why: Repeaters are invisible to sweeps written for title/editor (Ridgeline: service-page tabs kept impact-window copy).
check: Tab count before and after is equal; every tab_title changed is the planned one.

rule: Answer a question heading in the first sentence under it, and never name a service the client does not list or a price.
why: Beckett rulings on LCC (15 Sep 2026); Elevation answers cost as what drives the price, no number.
check: First sentence of each answer addresses the question; no service outside the services list; no $ figures.

rule: Write by element id and field; never string-replace raw _elementor_data.
why: Elementor stores curly apostrophes escaped so phrases silently fail to match, and phrase maps converted half a sentence on Ridgeline ("... or a screen for the lanai" on a fence site).
check: Every planned row names post id + element id + field; the tool decodes JSON, sets the field, re-encodes; zero raw str_replace on the meta string.

rule: Replace whole paragraphs, not fragments of sentences, and swap longer strings before shorter ones.
why: "Replace" to "Security" turned "Window Replacement" into "Window Securityment"; a phrase swap ate a tag and printed "Fort Myers./span>".
check: After the push, each changed field has balanced tags (count ) and contains the full planned paragraph.

rule: No em dashes in any copy you write; use a comma or a full stop.
why: House style; on rank-holding pages the em dash to comma swap is the one allowed edit to preserved paragraphs.
check: Rendered text of every touched page contains no U+2014.

rule: Use US spelling on US sites (color, neighborhood, license, center, gray, aluminum).
why: WesCo shipped "neighbourhoods" and "kerb"; Elevation needed a US spelling pass on pages and templates (13 Oct 2026).
check: language-audit British-spelling check returns zero on touched pages; swaps use word boundaries so class names and paths are untouched.

rule: Keep every ranking heading and the paragraphs under it word for word on a rank-holding site; only em dash to comma and Tamim-approved H1 edits are allowed.
why: Tamim's preserve rule (29 Sep 2026), used on Yard Dogs and Elevation.
check: Diff each preserved string from SEO-PRESERVE.md against the rendered page: identical except listed edits.

rule: Every number, warranty, award or claim must trace to something the client said; never invent or carry one over.
why: Ridgeline launched claiming 6,400 projects this year (Sunset's number) for a company founded in January; Elevation's warranty is 7-year, not lifetime.
check: Each number in new copy maps to a fact-gate row; counters checked in starting_number/ending_number/suffix too.

rule: If a field is bound to a dynamic tag (`__dynamic__`) or a global, writing the literal does nothing: change the source (esci_* option, ACF field) or remove the binding with Beckett's OK.
why: Yard Dogs contact boxes kept Sunshine's phone because a dynamic tag overrode the static text; buttons read "Get a Free Estimate" from esci_consultation_text.
check: Before writing, the tool checks the element for __dynamic__ / __globals__ on that field and routes or escalates.

rule: Copy that a client named exactly ships exactly; put any concern in one line after it, never a substitute.
why: Beckett (5 Oct 2026): his specific words are the spec.
check: Client-specified strings appear verbatim in the rendered page.

rule: Remove placeholder or hidden text instead of hiding it with CSS.
why: Pax (22 Dec 2025) was flagged by Amazon after launch for lorem ipsum in hidden sections.
check: No lorem/TODO/{{token}} in raw HTML, visible or not.

rule: Find text printed by CSS `content:` in the raw HTML and change only the quoted string, leaving every other CSS declaration byte for byte.
why: Ridgeline printed "Serving Southwest Florida" via ::after; Dobbins card labels read "See landscaping" from CSS.
check: grep raw HTML for `content:` on the touched page; only the quoted string changed in the diff.

rule: Treat sitewide text outside the main content (top bar, hidden tagline, footer NAP and hours, footer blurb) as ranking text too.
why: Beckett caught the "Volusia County and the Surrounding Areas" bar on Yard Dogs; the footer blurb is esci_footer_text, not Elementor.
check: The preserve and change lists include header, footer and option-sourced strings.

rule: Give each market, town or city page its own 150 to 300 word local paragraph; never repeat one paragraph across pages.
why: Tamim's thin-content rule (Elevation, 12 Oct 2026); many city pages from one template read as duplicate content.
check: Similarity between local paragraphs on any two pages stays low (no shared sentence).

rule: Use one link format per field (relative path or full URL, not both), and check hard-coded card and button links: publishing a page does not fix them.
why: ProWash built a doubled URL (site/free-quote/https://site/free-quote/); Sunshine card links were hard-coded "#".
check: Every href on touched pages resolves with one 200 and none is "#".

rule: Never link to a parked or unlaunched page.
why: Elevation (Oct 2026): pages built but not launching sit in one parked set and nothing may link to them.
check: Every internal href on a touched page returns 200 for a published page.

rule: Phone links are always `tel:+1` followed by ten digits.
why: Ridgeline's tel:+4237798436 and Sunset's tel:+1:2399202414 looked right on screen and dialled nowhere.
check: Regex on every tel: href: ^tel:\+1\d{10}$.

rule: Store _elementor_data with `wp_slash(wp_json_encode($data))` and validate the JSON before writing.
why: Elementor stores the meta slashed; writing it unslashed corrupts the page, and Elevation's scripts stop on invalid JSON.
check: json_decode of the stored meta succeeds after the write and the element count is unchanged.

rule: Dump every string setting of the page, including repeater arrays (items, tabs, slides, cards), before planning a change.
why: Six of Ridgeline's misses were repeater arrays, each named differently, that a title/editor sweep never saw.
check: The plan is built from a full dump, not from the editor's visible fields.

rule: Regenerate post_content after writing _elementor_data (regen-content.php).
why: post_content is a stale snapshot that site search, Rank Math meta and schema read; Dobbins search results showed donor text after a perfect fill (5 Oct 2026).
check: post_content of the touched post contains the new text after the push.

rule: Check globalTemplateID before assuming a section is shared: "global-looking" sections are often per-page copies that need every instance changed.
why: Sunshine's services cards were a per-page copy on 17 pages; editing the home page propagated nothing.
check: The plan lists every instance of the section by post id, or the one template id if it is truly global.

rule: On Legacy, Diamond and the OG template, service and city pages are ACF-driven (hero, sub-services, FAQ, workflow come from ACF fields); on the Sunshine-lineage FSO sites they live in _elementor_data. Edit the layer that renders.
why: Legacy's 73 service and city pages have zero page trees (one template #2254 + ACF); a Legacy hero imported empty because its copy is bound by ACF dynamic tags.
check: Before writing, the tool checks whether the target widget carries an acf dynamic tag; if so it writes the ACF field.

rule: After a structured write, scan the post for duplicate element ids.
why: A dangling foreach-by-reference variable overwrote a heading on 6 pages with a "4." step marker; the duplicate-id scan caught it.
check: elementor-repair.php duplicate-id report is empty for touched posts.

rule: Do not rename menus, terms or page slugs as part of a copy edit: Elementor's nav widget references menus by slug and silently falls back to the first menu.
why: Ridgeline (12 Aug 2026): a menu rename left all three footer columns showing the same four links.
check: No menu/term rename in the plan; if Beckett approves one, grep templates for the old slug afterwards.

rule: Some template sections are locked from the SEO editor or bound to fields; if a heading cannot be found in the page's own data, look in its template or ACF before concluding it is missing.
why: Cold Iron and the city-service template exposed only the hero, the next heading and the FAQ to the SEO team (Jun 2026).
check: Unfound strings are traced to a template id or ACF field in the report.

rule: Treat shared templates as site-wide edits: service areas 2478 (Sunset markets 6057, 6062, 6067, 6070), FAQ 9182 / 2873, header 14, footer 47, lead forms 9936 / 2535 / 2087; editing one changes every page that embeds it.
why: Beckett (23 Sep 2026): "you don't have to sweep 11 pages" for a string that lives in one template, and sweeping creates inconsistent copies.
check: Resolve each shortcode id on the page first; the scope report lists every page that embeds the template; verify on two of them after the push.

rule: Theme-builder templates apply by condition (single service #2254, city-service #2677, single project #1347, project archive #1146, blog archive #1411, single post #1457): an edit lands on every page of that type.
why: The HHL template set is one master template applied site-wide on Sunset and Legacy.
check: The plan names the template and the count of pages it renders.

rule: On Sunset, 2873 (Global FAQ) and 7732 (why choose us) are source templates not linked from live pages; the live pages hold their own copies.
why: Sunset microsite work (14 Oct 2026) found pages carrying duplicated copies with the same widget ids.
check: Search the page's own _elementor_data for the string before editing a library template.

rule: Per-page strings still need a per-page edit: H1s and their spans, "Recent work across X" strips, excerpts, Rank Math fields, ACF fields and esci page overrides.
why: Global-templates rule (LCC, 23 Sep 2026): only the template-held blocks are edit-once.
check: The plan separates template rows from page rows.

rule: Hide a header button with visibility:hidden, never display:none (escalate the CSS change).
why: Elevation (22 Oct 2026): display:none collapsed the flex row and slid the nav off-centre.
check: Header nav x-position at 1440 unchanged after the change.

rule: Keep unused template pages (city-service template, location template) in draft; never publish one.
why: A published city-service template page with excavation copy sat on a construction site until unpublished (7 May 2026).
check: No page titled like a template slug (city-service, template) is published.

rule: On Sunset-style multi-market sites every page of a market must carry its own stamps (_market_nav_menu, _market_footer_menu_1..3, _esci_page_phone, _esci_page_phone_tel, _esci_page_email, _esci_page_location); there is no inheritance.
why: Sunset (14 Oct 2026): menus were stamped but contact only on home and contact pages, so 108 service, about and city pages showed Fort Myers' phone.
check: market_audit.py prints ALL CONSISTENT after any edit on a multi-market site.

rule: Never put another market's phone, address, warranty or photos on a market page.
why: Elevation (Oct 2026): market tokens come from the page's market; lifetime warranty and Colorado exteriors never on Florida pages.
check: Crawl each market's pages for every other market's phone digits and address: zero hits.

rule: Know which chrome mechanism the site uses: Sunset = one header and footer plus per-page meta; Elevation = header and footer templates by URL section (display conditions).
why: Elevation chose display conditions so the market chrome cannot drift (13 Oct 2026); editing the wrong layer changes nothing.
check: The site config records the mechanism; the tool edits the matching layer.

rule: Body-copy phone numbers and emails are plain text, not from the contact plugin: update them by hand and audit for leaks.
why: Sunset bug list item 8 (Oct 2026).
check: market_audit.py leak check clean.

rule: On Elevation the WordPress front page is the Colorado page and /colorado/ 301s to /.
why: Set at launch (22 Oct 2026) so the home keeps the old home page's 85 rankings.
check: `wp option get page_on_front` returns the Colorado page id; /colorado/ returns one 301 to /.

rule: Market service-area blocks are market-wide templates (one per market), not one global.
why: Beckett (4 May 2026): a single global would show the wrong cities on other markets.
check: Each market page embeds its own market's service-area template id.

rule: Resolve every page by its path, never by "the front page" (page_on_front), and never re-push a drafted page.
why: Elevation (22 Oct 2026): push.php resolved the brand-home row as page_on_front after / was switched to Colorado, overwrote Colorado with the drafted home and / went 404.
check: Every row in the push names a path; the tool aborts if a row's target is page_on_front or post_status is draft.

rule: Never add or re-add a redirect for /blog or /contact to its trailing-slash form; WordPress already adds the slash and Rank Math strips it, which loops.
why: Elevation (Oct 2026): /blog to /blog/ looped and the redirect was deleted (rm-blog-redirect.php); /contact was dropped for the same reason.
check: curl -sIL on every redirect source: one 301 hop to a 200, never a cycle or more than 2 hops.

rule: Never change a slug yourself; if Beckett approves one, add a 301 from the old URL, keep _wp_old_slug, rewrite menu and breadcrumb links, and flush the sitemap cache.
why: Slug changes are URL changes; Ridgeline's /services-hub/ fix needed _wp_old_slug and link rewrites (12 Aug 2026).
check: Old URL returns 301 to the new one; no internal href points at the old slug.

rule: Redirects live in Rank Math's redirections table; after editing them delete the rank_math_redirections_cache transient.
why: Elevation's redirect fix cleared the transient so the change took effect.
check: The changed source returns the new status on a plain request.

rule: Keep existing URLs exactly and 301 every removed URL to its closest page.
why: Tamim's preserve rule; Elevation carried 30 redirects including old 2019 to 2021 WordPress URLs, junk URLs left 404.
check: Every old URL in the preserve 301 map returns one 301 to a 200.

rule: Alt text lives in two places, the widget's image.alt and the attachment's _wp_attachment_image_alt, and survives an image swap: set or clear both.
why: Ridgeline (12 Aug 2026) shipped 18 inline and 46 attachment alts describing palms and storm skies behind Tennessee fence photos.
check: Rendered alt of each touched image equals the planned alt; attachment meta matches.

rule: A page's featured image is the og:image fallback even when the page never shows it.
why: Yard Dogs (30 Sep 2026): featured images were donor photos and showed in the iMessage preview.
check: Every touched page has its own _thumbnail_id or an explicit rank_math_facebook_image_id.

rule: Never AI-edit, upscale or restore a client's real photos; geotag with the tool and name folders by project type and city, never street address.
why: Standing rule on real photos; Tamim's geotag and folder method (May to Jun 2026).
check: Uploaded file hash equals the original apart from EXIF geotag.

rule: The favicon is a PNG (512 square), never SVG or WebP, and Google takes days to show a new one.
why: Safari and iOS ignore SVG favicons; Google rejects WebP; Sunshine's favicon change took days (17 Aug 2026).
check: site_icon attachment mime is image/png.

rule: After replacing an SVG file, re-sync the attachment's _elementor_inline_svg meta.
why: Elementor inlines the meta, not the file; overwriting the .svg changed nothing twice in one day.
check: Rendered inline SVG equals the new file.

rule: Check privacy, terms and ADA pages for the client's own company name, phone (text and tel: link) and an email whose domain has MX; fix post_content as well as _elementor_data.
why: 22 Sep 2026: four live privacy policies named Sunshine State Hurricane Protection and a dead email domain; LCC showed WesCo's phone with Ridgeline's tel: link; donor text survived in post_content on three sites.
check: `scripts/legal-audit.py` prints ok for the site; `dig +short <domain> MX` is non-empty.

rule: Known open item: Bucktown's privacy page is unlinked and gives a dead-domain email (real: wade@bucktowngradingandconstruction.com) with two broken tel: links sitewide.
why: Blocked on the GHL key import (22 Sep 2026).
check: legal-audit.py row for Bucktown.

rule: Never touch MX, SPF, DKIM, DMARC or _domainconnect records; DNS changes beyond a verification TXT are Beckett's.
why: Losing them sends the client's mail to spam silently (WesCo migration, Sep 2026).
check: The only DNS write the tool may request is a google-site-verification TXT, approved.

rule: Verify Search Console by a DNS TXT record (send the value to Claude, it is added in Cloudflare), not a WordPress meta tag.
why: Linking GSC to GA4 needs a verified owner; full GSC user access was not enough (13 May 2026); Elevation's handover uses DNS.
check: `dig +short TXT <domain>` shows the google-site-verification value.

rule: The canonical host is always www with trailing slashes; the apex 301s to www.
why: Beckett (9 Oct 2026): "when we do domains, it's always www" (Dobbins went apex by mistake).
check: https://<apex>/ returns 301 to https://www.<domain>/; canonical tags use www.

rule: If a site "isn't loading" right after a DNS change, check negative DNS cache before touching anything.
why: Cloudflare's SOA negative TTL is 30 minutes; checking in the same minute poisons your own resolver.
check: dig works + curl fails + curl --resolve works means nothing is wrong with the site.

rule: Never edit form fields, recipients or webhooks; forms are the template's native Elementor forms and Beckett maps every webhook.
why: Yard Dogs forms posted into another client's GHL until rewired; a whole-page re-push nearly wiped mapped webhooks (30 Sep 2026).
check: No form widget settings in the push diff; clean-check area 17 still passes after the push.

rule: Fact-gate the text inside form templates (9936, 2087, 2535) like any other copy.
why: Dobbins (5 Oct 2026): the contact form promised "We'll get back to you within 2 hours. Guaranteed." from the donor.
check: Rendered form text has no claim missing from the fact gate.
